source.original_text: Let μ and ν be probability measures on a measurable parameter space W. Let Φ map W to a real Hilbert space H and be Bochner integrable under both laws, and let y be a fixed vector in H. Write m(ρ)=∫Φ dρ, R(ρ)=‖m(ρ)−y‖², and V(w)=2⟨m(μ)−y,Φ(w)⟩. For every 0≤t≤1, the actual positive measure ρₜ=(1−t)μ+tν is a probability, Φ is integrable under ρₜ, and its mean is the affine interpolation of the endpoint means. V is integrable under both endpoint laws. The right derivative of R(ρₜ) at zero is ∫V dν−∫V dμ. The exact remainder R(ν)−R(μ)−(∫V dν−∫V dμ) is ‖m(ν)−m(μ)‖², and is therefore nonnegative.

lean.statement:
theorem result
    {W H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (μ ν : Measure W) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (feature : W → H) (label : H)
    (hμ : Integrable feature μ) (hν : Integrable feature ν) :
    let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • μ + ENNReal.ofReal t • ν
    let mean : Measure W → H := fun law => ∫ w, feature w ∂law
    let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ‖mean law - label‖ ^ 2
    let potential : W → ℝ := fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ - label, feature w⟫_ℝ
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧ Integrable feature (curve t) ∧
      mean (curve t) = (1 - t) • mean μ + t • mean ν) ∧
    Integrable potential μ ∧ Integrable potential ν ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ))
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0 ∧
    (risk ν - risk μ - ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) =
      ‖mean ν - mean μ‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (risk μ + ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) ≤ risk ν)

blind_reconstruction.text: For every measurable space W, every complete real inner-product normed vector space H, every probability measures mu,nu on W, every feature:W->H, and fixed label:H, assume feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under mu and under nu. For every real t define the actual positive measure curve(t)=ofReal(1-t) times mu + ofReal(t) times nu, where ofReal(r) is the nonnegative extended-real coefficient max(r,0). For any measure law on W define mean(law)=integral_W feature(w) dlaw(w) in H and risk(law)=norm(mean(law)-label)^2 in R. Define the single scalar potential(w)=2*inner_product(mean(mu)-label,feature(w)). Abbreviate D=integral_W potential(w) dnu(w)-integral_W potential(w) dmu(w). Every integral is the literal Bochner integral over all W under the displayed measure; the potential integrals are real-valued. Then all of the following hold: (1) For every real t in the closed interval [0,1], curve(t) is a probability measure, feature is genuinely Bochner integrable under curve(t), and mean(curve(t))=(1-t) times mean(mu)+t times mean(nu). (2) potential is integrable under mu. (3) potential is integrable under nu. (4) The real function t->risk(curve(t)) has derivative D within the closed interval [0,1] at its endpoint 0, including the actual function value at 0. (5) risk(nu)-risk(mu)-D=norm(mean(nu)-mean(mu))^2. (6) risk(mu)+D<=risk(nu). The vector integrability assumptions are supplied separately under the two endpoint laws; segment integrability and both scalar potential integrability claims are derived. For t in [0,1] the nonnegative coefficients are exactly 1-t and t, and the endpoints are curve(0)=mu and curve(1)=nu, with the corresponding means and risks. The derivative is the right-hand endpoint derivative relative to the specified closed interval: as t approaches 0 through that interval, risk(curve(t))=risk(mu)+t*D+o(abs(t)). It is not a claim of an unrestricted two-sided derivative of this actual measure curve. Outside [0,1] the displayed definition still uses clipped nonnegative coefficients rather than a signed affine combination; probability and affine-mean conclusions are asserted only within [0,1]. The scalar difference D uses the same potential based at mean(mu) and is nu minus mu, never an integral against positive or truncated measure subtraction. Under the supplied integrability D also equals 2*inner_product(mean(mu)-label,mean(nu)-mean(mu)), but the explicit derivative value in the statement is the difference of the actual scalar integrals. The loss is the unhalved squared norm of the feature mean minus label, rather than an integral of pointwise squared residuals. The exact remainder is a nonnegative squared norm; D itself may have either sign. No feature second-moment hypothesis, pointwise continuity, topology on W, or abstract global first-variation assertion on measures is supplied or concluded.

open MeasureTheory
open scoped InnerProductSpace

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.ProbabilitySegmentRisk

theorem quadratic_feature_probability_segment
    {W H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace W]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (μ ν : Measure W) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (feature : W → H) (label : H)
    (hμ : Integrable feature μ) (hν : Integrable feature ν) :
    let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
      ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • μ + ENNReal.ofReal t • ν
    let mean : Measure W → H := fun law => ∫ w, feature w ∂law
    let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ‖mean law - label‖ ^ 2
    let potential : W → ℝ := fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ - label, feature w⟫_ℝ
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧ Integrable feature (curve t) ∧
      mean (curve t) = (1 - t) • mean μ + t • mean ν) ∧
    Integrable potential μ ∧ Integrable potential ν ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ))
      (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0 ∧
    (risk ν - risk μ - ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) =
      ‖mean ν - mean μ‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (risk μ + ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) ≤ risk ν) := by
  dsimp only
  let curve : ℝ → Measure W := fun t =>
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t) • μ + ENNReal.ofReal t • ν
  let mean : Measure W → H := fun law => ∫ w, feature w ∂law
  let risk : Measure W → ℝ := fun law => ‖mean law - label‖ ^ 2
  let potential : W → ℝ := fun w => 2 * ⟪mean μ - label, feature w⟫_ℝ
  change (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
    IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧ Integrable feature (curve t) ∧
    mean (curve t) = (1 - t) • mean μ + t • mean ν) ∧
    Integrable potential μ ∧ Integrable potential ν ∧
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => risk (curve t))
      ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) 0 ∧
    (risk ν - risk μ - ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) =
      ‖mean ν - mean μ‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (risk μ + ((∫ w, potential w ∂ν) - (∫ w, potential w ∂μ)) ≤ risk ν)
  have hprops : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
      IsProbabilityMeasure (curve t) ∧ Integrable feature (curve t) ∧
      mean (curve t) = (1 - t) • mean μ + t • mean ν := by
    intro t ht
    have hleft : 0 ≤ 1 - t := sub_nonneg.mpr ht.2
    have hμt := hμ.smul_measure (c := ENNReal.ofReal (1 - t)) ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
    have hνt := hν.smul_measure (c := ENNReal.ofReal t) ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
    refine ⟨?_, hμt.add_measure hνt, ?_⟩
    · apply isProbabilityMeasure_iff.mpr
      simp only [curve, Measure.add_apply, Measure.smul_apply, measure_univ, smul_eq_mul,
        mul_one]
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_add hleft ht.1]
      norm_num
    · dsimp only [mean, curve]
      rw [integral_add_measure hμt hνt, integral_smul_measure, integral_smul_measure,
        ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hleft, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal ht.1]
  have hcalc := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticFeatureRisk.quadratic_feature_mean_calculus
    μ ν feature label hμ hν
  dsimp only at hcalc
  rcases hcalc with ⟨hpotμ, hpotν, hpair, hbre, hsupport, hderiv⟩
  refine ⟨hprops, hpotμ, hpotν, ?_, hbre, hsupport⟩
  apply hderiv.hasDerivWithinAt.congr_of_mem
  · intro t ht
    change ‖mean (curve t) - label‖ ^ 2 = _
    rw [(hprops t ht).2.2]
    congr 2
    rw [sub_smul, one_smul, smul_sub]
    abel
  · exact ⟨le_rfl, zero_le_one⟩


end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.ProbabilitySegmentRisk

steps.title: Stay within probability measures
steps.text: On the closed interval the two nonnegative coefficients add to one. Scaling and adding genuine integrable functions preserves integrability under the resulting measure.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Integrate the affine segment
steps.text: Linearity of the Bochner integral identifies the actual segment mean, without replacing the measure path by an unrelated vector path.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Compute the potential pairing
steps.text: The bounded linear functional defined by the fixed residual commutes with the integral. This also proves the two scalar potential integrals exist.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Differentiate and retain the square remainder
steps.text: Apply real Hilbert-space squared-norm calculus to the affine mean. Restrict its derivative to the probability interval; expand the square to obtain the nonnegative remainder.
